content: खालील वाक्यातील प्रयोग ओळखा. कृष्ण बासरी वाजवतो.
explanation:
'कृष्ण बासरी वाजवतो' या वाक्यात कर्ता (कृष्ण) महत्त्वाचा आहे आणि क्रियापदाचे लिंग, वचन कर्त्यानुसार बदलते (उदा. 'राधा बासरी वाजवते'). म्हणून हा 'कर्तरी प्रयोग' आहे.
कर्तरी प्रयोगाचे प्रकार
कर्तरी प्रयोगाचे दोन उपप्रकार पडतात:
१. सकर्मक कर्तरी प्रयोग
ज्या कर्तरी प्रयोगाच्या वाक्यात 'कर्म' अ+सते, त्याला सकर्मक कर्तरी प्रयोग म्हणतात.
उदाहरणे:
राम आंबा खातो. (राम - कर्ता, आंबा - कर्म. राम ऐवजी 'सीता' घेतल्यास क्रियापद 'खाते' असे बदलते.)
ती गाणे गाते.
मुले क्रिकेट खेळतात.
२. अकर्मक कर्तरी प्रयोग
ज्या कर्तरी प्रयोगाच्या वाक्यात 'कर्म' नसते, त्याला अकर्मक कर्तरी प्रयोग म्हणतात.
उदाहरणे:
तो हसतो. (कर्म नाही. तो ऐवजी 'ती' घेतल्यास 'हसते' होते.)
पक्षी आकाशात उडतो. ('आकाशात' हे कर्म नसून स्थळ/अधिकरण आहे. उडणारा कोण? पक्षी - कर्ता).
मी रस्त्यात पडलो.
परीक्षेसाठी खास टीप (Pro-Tip)
प्रयोगाचा कोणताही प्रश्न सोडवताना सर्वात आधी वाक्यातील कर्ता शोधा.
कर्ता शोधण्यासाठी क्रियापदाच्या मूळ रूपाला (धातुला) 'णारा / णारी / णारे कोण?' असा प्रश्न विचारा.
सापडलेल्या कर्त्याला जर कोणताही प्रत्यय लागलेला नसेल, तर तो डोळे झाकून 'कर्तरी प्रयोग' असतो!

content: खालील म्हणीचा योग्य अर्थ ओळखा. उतावळा नवरा गुडघ्याला बाशिग
explanation:
'उतावळा नवरा गुडघ्याला बाशिंग' या म्हणीचा अर्थ म्हणजे, एखाद्या व्यक्तीने अतिशय घाईने, उतावळेपणाने मूर्खपणाचे वर्तन करणे. बाशिंग हे डोक्याला बांधले जाते, गुडघ्याला नाही.
important:
बिगारीचे घोडे, तरवटाचा फोक - दुसऱ्याच्या वस्तूची सहजासहजी काळजी कोणी घेत नाही. 
पळसाला पाने तीनच: सगळीकडे सारखीच परिस्थिती.
बळी तो कान पिळी: बलवान माणूस इतरांवर हुकमत गाजवतो.
भित्यापाठी ब्रह्मराक्षस: भित्रा माणूस एखाद्या गोष्टीला घाबरत असेल तर नेमकी तीच गोष्ट सतत समोर येते.

content: खालील शब्दाचा विरूध्दार्थी शब्द ओळखा. जागृती
explanation: 'जागृती' म्हणजे जागे असणे, तर त्याचा विरुद्धार्थी शब्द 'निद्रा' म्हणजे झोप. 'प्रगती', 'विकृती', 'संस्कृती' हे संबंधित नाहीत.

content: खालील वाक्प्रचाराचा योग्य अर्थ ओळखा. हातावर तुरी देणे
explanation:
'हातावर तुरी देणे' या वाक्प्रचाराचा अर्थ 'फसवून पळून जाणे' किंवा 'डोळ्यात धूळ फेकून निसटणे' असा होतो.
महत्वाचे :
नारळ फुटणे - एखाद्या कार्यांचा शुभारंभ होणे 
नारळ हाती देणे - काहीही न देता निरोप देणे

content: खालील वाक्प्रचाराचा योग्य अर्थ ओळखा. विडा उचलणे
explanation:
'विडा उचलणे' म्हणजे एखादे कार्य करण्याची जबाबदारी स्वीकारणे किंवा 'प्रतिज्ञा करणे'.
महत्वाचे :
धुळीस मिळणे - सर्वनाश होणे
नक्राश्रू ढाळणे - खोटे दुःख दाखविणे

content: खालील शब्दाचा समास ओळखा. रस्तोरस्ती
explanation:
'रस्तोरस्ती' हा 'अव्ययीभाव समास' आहे. या समासात पहिले पद महत्त्वाचे असते आणि त्याची पुनरावृत्ती होते, जसे की 'घरोघरी', 'दारोदारी'
अव्ययीभाव समास (लक्षणे आणि व्याख्या)
व्याख्या: ज्या समासात पहिले पद (शब्द) महत्त्वाचे (प्रधान) असते आणि तयार झालेला जोडशब्द (सामासिक शब्द) वाक्यात क्रियाविशेषण अव्ययाचे काम करतो, त्याला 'अव्ययीभाव समास' असे म्हणतात.
ओळखण्याची मुख्य खूण: या समासातील शब्दांची सुरुवात बहुधा आ, यथा, प्रति, दर, हर, बे, बिन, गैर यांसारख्या उपसर्गांनी होते किंवा एकाच शब्दाची द्विरुक्ती (पुनरावृत्ती) झालेली असते..
जेव्हा एखाद्या मराठी शब्दाची द्विरुक्ती होऊन जोडशब्द तयार होतो आणि तो क्रियाविशेषणासारखा वापरला जातो, तेव्हा तो अव्ययीभाव समास असतो. (परीक्षेत यावर अनेकदा प्रश्न विचारले जातात.)
घरोघरी = प्रत्येक घरात
दारोदार = प्रत्येक दारी
गावोगाव = प्रत्येक गावात
गल्लोगल्ली = प्रत्येक गल्लीत
पावलोपावली = प्रत्येक पाऊलावर

content: खालील शब्दाचा समानार्थी शब्द ओळखा. शंका
explanation:
'शंका' या शब्दाचा समानार्थी शब्द 'संदेह' आहे. दोन्ही शब्दांचा अर्थ 'doubt' किंवा 'uncertainty' असा होतो.

महत्वाचे :
भगुर - नश्वर, क्षणिक, अशाश्वत 
भूषण - अलंकार, आमरण, दागिना,
भुरळ - मोहिनी, भ्रम, मोह,

content: खालील वाक्प्रचाराचा योग्य अर्थ ओळखा. वाट लावणे.
explanation:
'वाट लावणे' या वाक्प्रचाराचा अर्थ 'नाश करणे' किंवा 'एखादी गोष्ट वाईट स्थितीला आणणे' असा होतो
महत्वाचे :
दाती बळ धरणे - अतोनात मेहनत करणे
दुकान माजवणे - दंगा मांडणे 
धरणे धरून बसणे - हट्ट धरून बसंणे
धरमधक्का बसणे - व्यर्थ खटाटोप करावा लागणे

content: खालील म्हणीचा योग्य अर्थ ओळखा. केर डोळ्यात फुंकर कानात
explanation:
'केर डोळ्यात फुंकर कानात' या म्हणीचा अर्थ असा की, योग्य समस्या सोडून भलत्याच ठिकाणी किंवा चुकीच्या पद्धतीने उपाययोजना करणे.
महत्वाचे :
भिंतीस कान, दारास डोळे - कोणतीच गोष्ट गुपत राहत नाही. 
भिकाऱ्याच्या पोराला ओकारी फार - जो भिकेचे खातो त्याला मस्ती फार येते. 
मऊ असले म्हणून कोपराने खणू नये - एखाद्याच्या चांगुलपणाचा गैरफायदा घेऊ नये.

content: The committee decided to postpone the meeting ______ further notice.
explanation: The correct preposition to use in this context is 'until'. 'Until further notice' is a common idiom meaning indefinitely until a new announcement is made. 'Till' can also be used, but 'until' is generally preferred in formal writing. 'By' or 'for' do not fit the meaning.

content: If I ______ a bird, I would fly to distant lands.
explanation: This is a second conditional sentence expressing an unreal or hypothetical situation in the present or future. For hypothetical statements involving 'to be', 'were' is used for all persons (I, he, she, it) in the 'if' clause. Thus, 'If I were a bird' is correct.

content: The children were warned not to ______ with fire.
explanation: 'To play with fire' is an idiom meaning to take foolish risks. 'Meddle' means to interfere, 'tamper' means to interfere with something in order to cause damage or make unauthorized alterations, and 'fumble' means to handle clumsily.

content: She arrived at the station just ______ time to catch her train.
explanation: 'In time' means early enough, or before the last moment. 'On time' means at the scheduled time. Since she 'caught her train', she arrived early enough, not necessarily exactly at the scheduled time, making 'in time' the more appropriate choice.

content: The manager decided to ______ the meeting until the following week.
explanation: 'Adjourn' means to break off (a meeting, legal case, or game) with the intention of resuming it later. 'Postpone' is a synonym, but 'adjourn' is specifically used for meetings/proceedings. 'Defer' means to put off to a later time, 'cancel' means to call off entirely, and 'conclude' means to bring to an end.

content: He prefers coffee ______ tea.
explanation: The verb 'prefer' is typically followed by the preposition 'to' when comparing two nouns. For example, 'I prefer X to Y'.

content: The company is planning to ______ its operations to other countries.
explanation: 'Expand' means to increase in size, number, or importance. This fits the context of growing a company's operations. 'Contract' is the opposite, 'restrict' means to limit, and 'diminish' means to make or become less.

content: Hard work is ______ to success.
explanation: 'Indispensable' means absolutely necessary. Hard work is a crucial factor for success. 'Detrimental' means harmful, 'irrelevant' means not connected, and 'superfluous' means unnecessary.

content: The author's latest book is a ______ success.
explanation: 'Resounding' means unmistakable, emphatic, or loud. In the context of success, it means very great or impressive. 'Whispering' and 'faint' imply a small or weak success, while 'mute' means silent.

content: I complimented her ______ her beautiful dress.
explanation: The correct preposition to use with 'compliment' when referring to the reason for the compliment is 'on'. 'Compliment someone on something'.

content: The detective found a crucial ______ of evidence at the crime scene.
explanation: A 'piece' of evidence is the correct colocation. 'Section', 'fragment', and 'portion' can refer to parts of something, but 'piece of evidence' is the standard phrase.

content: Despite her best efforts, she could not ______ the jury of her innocence.
explanation: To 'convince' someone means to persuade them that something is true. 'Persuade' is also similar but 'convince' fits better with 'of her innocence'. 'Assure' means to tell someone something confidently, 'explain' means to make something clear, and 'inform' means to give facts or information.

content: He ______ to be a doctor, but fate had other plans.
explanation: 'Aspirated' means to breathe in, 'desired' is a general wish. 'Aspired' means to direct one's hopes or ambitions towards achieving something, which perfectly fits the context of wanting to become a doctor. 'Longed' also expresses a strong desire, but 'aspired' is more common when talking about professional goals.

content: The criminal was finally ______ after a long chase.
explanation: 'Apprehended' means arrested, which is the most appropriate term for catching a criminal. 'Captured' is also possible, but 'apprehended' is more formal and commonly used in a legal context. 'Seized' means taken hold of suddenly, and 'trapped' means caught in a trap.

content: It is difficult to ______ true happiness in material possessions.
explanation: 'Find' or 'seek' are appropriate here. 'Seek' implies a more active search or quest. 'Discover' implies finding something previously unknown. 'Create' means to bring into existence. 'Seek' conveys the idea of trying to find happiness, which is a common human endeavor.

content: The manager's decision was ______ with general approval from the staff.
explanation: 'Met with' is the correct phrasal verb meaning to be received with or to experience a particular reaction. 'Faced with' implies confronting a challenge, 'dealt with' implies handling a situation, and 'came with' means accompanied by.

content: Despite facing numerous challenges, the team remained ______ to their goal.
explanation: 'Dedicated' means devoted to a task or purpose. This fits the context of maintaining focus on a goal despite difficulties. 'Indifferent' means having no particular interest, 'apathetic' means showing no emotion, and 'hesitant' means unsure or reluctant.

content: It is essential to have a ______ diet for good health.
explanation: 'Balanced' means having all its parts in the correct proportions. A 'balanced diet' contains the right amount of various nutrients necessary for health. 'Rich' means abundant, 'heavy' implies large or difficult to digest, and 'limited' implies restricted.

content: If he ______ harder, he would have passed the exam.
explanation: This is a third conditional sentence, used to talk about hypothetical situations in the past. The structure is 'If + past perfect, would have + past participle'. Therefore, 'had studied' is the correct form.

content: The old house, with its crumbling walls and broken windows, had a ______ appearance.
explanation: The context of 'crumbling walls and broken windows' suggests a run-down or decaying state. 'Decrepit' means old and in poor condition. 'Vibrant' means full of energy, 'magnificent' means very impressive, and 'pristine' means perfectly clean and unspoiled.

content: Neither the students ______ the teacher was present at the meeting.
explanation: When 'neither... nor' is used, the verb agrees with the noun closest to it. Here, 'the teacher' (singular) is closer to the verb, so the singular verb 'was' is correct.

content: She has been working on this project ______ dawn.
explanation: 'Since' is used to indicate a starting point in time for an action that continues up to the present. 'From' typically indicates a starting point for an action that has a clear end or is part of a sequence. 'For' indicates duration, and 'at' is used for specific points in time.

content: The company's profits have been ______ steadily over the past quarter.
explanation: 'Declining' means decreasing, which fits the context of profits. 'Ascending' means increasing, 'advancing' means moving forward, and 'elevating' means raising to a higher position. The sentence implies a negative trend.

content: He is averse ______ hard work.
explanation: The phrasal verb 'averse to' means having a strong dislike of or opposition to something. It is always followed by the preposition 'to'.

content: The news was so ______ that it left everyone speechless.
explanation: 'Astonishing' means extremely surprising or impressive, which would naturally leave people speechless. 'Ordinary' means common, 'insignificant' means unimportant, and 'predictable' means expected.

content: The internet has revolutionized our lives in countless ways. It has become an ________ part of modern existence, connecting people across the globe and providing access to an enormous wealth of information.
explanation: The context describes the internet's widespread and indispensable role. 'Essential' means absolutely necessary or important, which perfectly fits this description. 'Dispensable' and 'optional' are antonyms, and 'superficial' means shallow, neither of which makes sense here.

content: Ultimately, the internet is a powerful tool, but its positive impact ________ heavily on how responsibly we use it.
explanation: The positive impact of the internet is dependent on how it is used. 'Relies on' means to be dependent on or to need something. 'Detaches,' 'disregards,' and 'ignores' do not convey the sense of dependence required by the context.

content: The internet has revolutionized our lives in countless ways. It has become an essential part of modern existence, connecting people across the globe and ________ access to an enormous wealth of information.
explanation: The internet's function is to make information available. 'Providing' means to make something available or supply something. 'Denying,' 'restricting,' and 'hindering' all imply limiting or blocking access, which is contrary to the internet's role in this positive context.

content: However, this convenience also ________ with it certain challenges. Cybercrime and data privacy are growing concerns, and the constant digital input can lead to information overload.
explanation: The phrasal verb 'bring with it' means to cause or introduce something as a consequence or accompanying feature. In this context, convenience 'causes' or 'introduces' challenges. 'Takes,' 'leaves,' and 'goes' do not form a meaningful idiomatic expression here.

content: However, this convenience also brings with it certain challenges. Cybercrime and data privacy are growing ________, and the constant digital input can lead to information overload.
explanation: Cybercrime and data privacy are negative issues that cause worry. 'Concerns' refers to matters of interest or worry. 'Solutions,' 'opportunities,' and 'advantages' are positive terms and do not fit the context of 'challenges' mentioned earlier.

content: Cybercrime and data privacy are growing concerns, and the constant digital ________ can lead to information overload. While the internet offers immense potentials for education and business, users must exercise caution when navigating its vast landscape.
explanation: 'Information overload' is caused by receiving too much information. 'Input' refers to information that is put into a system or received by a person. 'Silence' and 'withdrawal' are the opposite, and 'output' refers to information sent out.

content: While the internet offers immense ________ for education and business, users must exercise caution when navigating its vast landscape.
explanation: The sentence starts with 'While,' indicating a contrast with the challenges previously mentioned. Thus, a positive aspect is needed. 'Potentials' refers to the capabilities or possibilities for growth and development. 'Obstacles,' 'drawbacks,' and 'hindrances' are negative terms, which contradict the positive intent here.

content: While the internet offers immense potentials for education and business, users must exercise ________ when navigating its vast landscape. It is crucial to be mindful of phishing scams and malicious software.
explanation: Given the risks (scams, malicious software) associated with the internet, users need to be careful and prudent. 'Caution' means care taken to avoid danger or mistakes. 'Recklessness,' 'indifference,' and 'ignorance' all suggest a lack of care or awareness.

content: It is crucial to be ________ of phishing scams and malicious software. Furthermore, striking a balance between online and offline activities is essential for overall well-being.
explanation: To protect oneself from scams, one must be aware and vigilant. 'Mindful' means conscious or aware of something. 'Unaware,' 'ignorant,' and 'negligent' are antonyms, suggesting a lack of awareness or care.

content: Furthermore, striking a balance ________ online and offline activities is essential for overall well-being. Ultimately, the internet is a powerful tool, but its positive impact relies heavily on how responsibly we use it.
explanation: When referring to a relationship or comparison involving two distinct entities (online activities and offline activities), the preposition 'between' is typically used. 'Among' is used for three or more items. 'With' and 'for' do not fit the idiomatic expression 'balance between'.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Honesty** is the best policy.
explanation:
''Honesty'' is an abstract noun. Nouns are fundamental parts of speech that name people, places, things, or ideas. Abstract nouns specifically refer to concepts, qualities, or states that cannot be physically perceived, such as 'honesty', 'love', 'freedom', or 'happiness'. In this sentence, 'honesty' functions as the subject, which is a common role for nouns, demonstrating a key characteristic or quality.
Rule 4: Always Plural Some nouns exist only in plural form because they consist of two identical parts. They take a plural verb.
Important Words: Scissors, Trousers, Spectacles, Pants, Binoculars.
Exam Error: Where is my spectacles? (❌)
Correction: Where are my spectacles? (✅)
Rule 5: Hyphenated Nouns A hyphenated noun is never used in the plural form.
Exam Error: He gave me a five-rupees note. (❌)
Correction: He gave me a five-rupee note. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: A **flock** of birds flew across the clear blue sky.
explanation:
'Flock' is a collective noun representing a group of birds. Nouns are words that name a person, place, thing, or idea. Collective nouns are a specific type of noun that refers to a group of individuals or items, treated as a single unit. Other examples include 'team,' 'committee,' 'herd,' and 'family,' which name a collection of entities.
Rule 2: Look Plural, Act Singular Some nouns end in "s" and look plural, but they are singular in meaning and take a singular verb.
Important Words: News, Mathematics, Physics, Politics, Innings, Summons.
Exam Error: Mathematics are a difficult subject. (❌)
Correction: Mathematics is a difficult subject. (✅)
Rule 3: Look Singular, Act Plural Some nouns look singular but represent a group and always take a plural verb. Never add "s" to these words.
Important Words: Cattle, Police, Poultry, Peasantry, People.
Exam Error: The cattles are grazing. / The cattle is grazing. (❌)
Correction: The cattle are grazing. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The man **who** called you yesterday is my uncle.
explanation:
'Who' acts as a relative pronoun, connecting the dependent clause 'who called you yesterday' to the noun 'man' and referring back to it. Relative pronouns (e.g., who, whom, whose, which, that) introduce relative clauses, which provide additional information about a noun or pronoun in the main clause. They also function as a subject or object within their own clause.
Golden Rules for Exams (Spotting Errors & Sentence Improvement)
Pronouns are a massive scoring area for SSC and Talathi exams. The rules below are tested repeatedly.
Rule 1: The "231" and "123" Rule (Order of Pronouns)
When three pronouns (First Person - I/We, Second Person - You, Third Person - He/She/They) are used in the same sentence, their order depends on the meaning of the sentence.
Positive Sense (Good acts): The order should be 231 (Second, Third, First).
Exam Error: I, you, and he are going to the party. (❌)
Correction: You, he, and I are going to the party. (✅)
Negative Sense (Confession/Mistake): The order should be 123 (First, Second, Third).
Exam Error: You, he, and I made a huge mistake. (❌)
Correction: I, you, and he made a huge mistake. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: She sings **beautifully** at the annual function.
explanation:
'Beautifully' modifies the verb 'sings,' telling us the manner in which she sings. This classifies it as an adverb. Adverbs are words that modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, providing details about how, when, where, or to what extent an action or description occurs. Many adverbs of manner, like 'beautifully,' end in -ly.

 Confusing Adverbs (Exam Favorites)
Examiners love to test the difference between these pairs.
Hard vs. Hardly:
Hard: With a lot of effort (Adverb of manner).
Hardly: Almost not / rarely (Adverb of frequency).
Exam Error: He works hardly to pass the exam. (❌)
Correction: He works hard to pass the exam. (✅)
Late vs. Lately:
Late: After the usual or expected time.
Lately: Recently.
Exam Error: Have you seen him late? (❌)
Correction: Have you seen him lately? (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: This is a **beautiful** house near the river.
explanation:
'Beautiful' describes the noun 'house,' telling us about its quality. Therefore, it is an adjective. Adjectives are words that modify or describe nouns or pronouns, adding detail and specificity. They provide information about attributes like color, size, shape, or, in this case, aesthetic quality, enhancing the noun's meaning.
Rule 1: The "IOR" Rule (Strictly takes 'To')
Latin adjectives ending in -ior—such as senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior, anterior, posterior—are always followed by to, never by than.
Exam Error: He is senior than me in the office. (❌)
Correction: He is senior to me in the office. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: Please wait in the lobby **until** the rain stops.
explanation:
'Until' connects the main clause 'Please wait in the lobby' with the dependent time clause 'the rain stops.' This linking function makes it a conjunction. Specifically, it's a subordinating conjunction, which introduces a dependent clause and links it to an independent clause, establishing a relationship of time, cause, condition, or concession between them.

Rule 1: Fixed Correlative Pairs
Never mix and match these pairs. Examiners frequently swap the second word to create an error.
Either is followed by or
Neither is followed by nor
Not only is followed by but also
Both is followed by and (Never use 'as well as' with 'both')
Exam Error: He is both smart as well as hardworking. (❌)
Correction: He is both smart and hardworking. (✅)
Rule 2: The "No Sooner" Rule
"No sooner" is strictly followed by than (not 'then' or 'when'). It also requires an inverted verb structure (auxiliary verb before the subject).
Structure: No sooner + had/did + Subject + verb + than + Subject + verb.
Exam Error: No sooner did I reach the station when the train left. (❌)
Correction: No sooner did I reach the station than the train left. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The brave boy jumped **into** the flowing river.
explanation: 'Into' shows the direction and movement of the action 'jumped' relative to the 'river,' indicating entry. This identifies it as a preposition. Prepositions are words that establish relationships, particularly of position, direction, or time, between a noun or pronoun and other words in a sentence. They typically form a prepositional phrase with their object.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The street dog **barked** loudly at the stranger.
explanation:
'Barked' represents the action performed by the subject (the street dog). This clearly marks it as a verb. Verbs are crucial elements in a sentence that express actions, occurrences, or states of being. They change form to indicate tense (past, present, future), mood, and voice, conveying what the subject is doing or experiencing.
Rule 1: The "First Subject" Rule
When two subjects are joined by words like as well as, along with, together with, besides, in addition to, or with, the verb must agree with the first subject.
Exam Error: The captain along with the players are going to the field. (❌)
Correction: The captain along with the players is going to the field. (✅) (Because the first subject, "captain," is singular).

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Wow!** That is a stunning piece of architecture.
explanation:
'Wow' is used to express sudden amazement or wonder. This function is characteristic of an interjection. Interjections are exclamatory words or phrases that convey strong emotions or sudden reactions. They are grammatically independent of the rest of the sentence and are often followed by an exclamation mark, adding emphasis to a speaker's feeling.
Common Types of Interjections
For Joy: Hurrah, Wow, Yippee (e.g., Hurrah! We won.)
For Sorrow/Grief: Alas, Oh, Ouch (e.g., Alas! He is no more.)
For Surprise: What, Oh, Ah, Ha (e.g., What! You failed the test?)
For Approval/Praise: Bravo, Brilliant, Well done (e.g., Bravo! You played well.)
For Attention: Hush, Listen, Behold (e.g., Hush! The baby is sleeping.)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: She is **the** smartest girl in the entire class.
explanation: 'The' is a definite article used to point out a specific noun ('smartest girl'). Articles are a subclass of determiners (or adjectives) that specify whether a noun is general or specific. 'The' refers to a particular, known, or previously mentioned noun, making it distinct from the indefinite articles 'a' and 'an' which refer to non-specific items.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The **committee** has reached a final decision.
explanation:
'Committee' is a collective noun representing a group of people appointed for a specific function, treated as a single unit. Nouns are words that name a person, place, thing, or idea. Collective nouns are unique in that they refer to a collection of individuals or things, even though they appear in singular form and often take a singular verb, emphasizing the group as one entity.
Rule 1: Uncountable Nouns (Always Singular)
Certain nouns are uncountable and always take a singular verb. You cannot add "s" or "es" to them, nor can you use "a/an" before them.
Important Words: Scenery, Furniture, Advice, Information, Luggage, Baggage, Poetry, Machinery, Hair, Alphabet.
Exam Error: The sceneries of Kashmir are beautiful. (❌)
Correction: The scenery of Kashmir is beautiful. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: Usain Bolt is a **fast** runner.
explanation: Here, 'fast' describes the noun 'runner,' indicating a quality of the runner. Therefore, it functions as an adjective. Adjectives are words that modify or describe nouns or pronouns, providing more information about their characteristics, quantity, or state. They answer questions like 'which one?', 'what kind?', or 'how many?' regarding the noun they modify.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Someone** is knocking continuously at the door.
explanation:
'Someone' is an indefinite pronoun, referring to an unspecified person. Pronouns are words that substitute for nouns, helping to avoid repetition. Indefinite pronouns like 'someone,' 'anyone,' 'everyone,' 'nothing,' 'all,' or 'some' do not refer to a specific person, place, or thing, instead indicating a general or non-specific entity.
1. What is a Pronoun?
A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun to avoid repeating the noun. (In Marathi grammar, this is equivalent to सर्वनाम - Sarvanam).
Types of Pronouns
Personal Pronouns: Represent specific people or things (e.g., I, you, he, she, it, we, they).
Demonstrative Pronouns: Point to specific things (e.g., this, that, these, those).
Relative Pronouns: Connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun (e.g., who, whom, whose, which, that).
Reflexive Pronouns: Used when the subject and the object of a verb are the same person or thing (e.g., myself, yourself, himself).
Indefinite Pronouns: Refer to non-specific people or things (e.g., someone, anybody, everything, none)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: I checked my wallet, but I don't have **any** money left.
explanation:
. What is an Adjective?
An adjective is a describing word. It modifies or provides more information about a noun or a pronoun. (In Marathi grammar, this is equivalent to विशेषण - Visheshan).
Example: He is a brave soldier. (What kind of soldier? Brave.)
Example: I have five pens. (How many pens? Five.)

2. Degrees of Comparison
Adjectives change their form to show comparison.
Positive Degree: Used when no comparison is made (e.g., tall, beautiful).
Comparative Degree: Used to compare two people or things. Usually ends in -er or uses more (e.g., taller, more beautiful). It is generally followed by the word than.
Superlative Degree: Used to compare more than two people or things. Usually ends in -est or uses most (e.g., tallest, most beautiful). It is always preceded by the article the.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: She **hardly** studies for her semester exams.
explanation:
'Hardly' is an adverb of frequency or degree, modifying the verb 'studies' and indicating the extent or infrequency of the action. Adverbs are words that modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, providing information about how, when, where, or to what degree something happens. Adverbs of frequency, like 'hardly,' 'never,' 'always,' or 'often,' tell us how often an action occurs.
Rule 1: The "Enough" Rule
The placement of the word "enough" depends on what it is describing.

With Adjectives/Adverbs: It is placed after the word it modifies.
With Nouns: It is placed before the noun.
Exam Error: He is enough smart to crack the Talathi exam. (❌)
Correction: He is smart enough to crack the Talathi exam. (✅)
Noun Example: I have enough money to buy this book. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The passenger plane flew **over** the thick clouds.
explanation: 'Over' shows the positional relationship between the plane and the clouds, indicating that the plane was above them. This identifies it as a preposition. Prepositions are words that connect a noun or pronoun (the object of the preposition) to another word in the sentence, typically expressing relationships of space, time, or direction. They form prepositional phrases.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Although** he was terribly tired, he kept working.
explanation:
'Although' is a subordinating conjunction that links the dependent clause 'he was terribly tired' to the independent clause 'he kept working,' indicating a concession or contrast. 
Types of Conjunctions
Coordinating Conjunctions: Connect items of equal grammatical rank.
Trick to remember: FANBOYS (For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So).
Subordinating Conjunctions: Connect an independent clause to a dependent clause (e.g., because, although, if, unless, since).
Correlative Conjunctions: Conjunctions that are always used in pairs (e.g., either...or, both...and).

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: My brother wants to become a **doctor**.
explanation:
'Doctor' is a common noun that names a person in a particular profession. Nouns are fundamental parts of speech that identify people, places, things, or ideas. .
Types of Nouns
Proper Noun: Specific name of a person, place, or thing. Always capitalized. (e.g., India, Shivaji, Ganga)

Common Noun: General name for a class of persons, places, or things. (e.g., boy, city, river)

Collective Noun: A name given to a group or collection. (e.g., team, jury, army, committee)

Material Noun: Name of a substance or material. (e.g., gold, water, wood, iron)

Abstract Noun: Name of a quality, state, or concept that cannot be touched or seen. (e.g., bravery, childhood, honesty)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: He runs very **fast** during the final lap.
explanation:
In this context, 'fast' modifies the verb 'runs,' telling us *how* he runs. This makes it an adverb. Adverbs are words that modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, providing information about manner, place, time, frequency, or degree. They often answer questions like 'how?', 'when?', 'where?', or 'to what extent?' in a sentence.
Rule 2: The Double Negative Rule
Words like seldom, nowhere, never, nothing, hardly, scarcely, barely, and rarely already have a negative meaning. You must never use "not" or another negative word with them in the same clause.
* Exam Error: I hardly know nothing about this topic. (❌)
* Correction: I hardly know anything about this topic. (✅)
Rule 3: Rule of Inversion
When a sentence begins with a negative adverb (like Seldom, Never, Hardly, Scarcely, No sooner), the sentence must follow an inverted structure. This means the helping verb comes before the subject (just like in a question).
Structure: Negative Adverb + Helping Verb + Subject + Main Verb
Exam Error: Seldom he visits his native village. (❌)
Correction: Seldom does he visit his native village. (✅)
Exam Error: Never I have seen such a mess. (❌)
Correction: Never have I seen such a mess. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: She **has** completed her assignment on time.
explanation:
'Has' acts as a helping (auxiliary) verb here, supporting the main verb 'completed' to form the present perfect tense. Verbs are words that express an action, occurrence, or state of being. Auxiliary verbs like 'has,' 'is,' 'do,' 'will,' etc., combine with main verbs to form various tenses, moods, and voices, adding nuance to the action.
Rule 2: The "Nearest Subject" Rule
When two subjects are joined by either...or, neither...nor, not only...but also, or simply or/nor, the verb must agree with the subject closest to it.
Exam Error: Neither the teacher nor the students is present. (❌)
Correction: Neither the teacher nor the students are present. (✅) (Because "students", which is plural, is closest to the verb).

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The children are playing **in** the garden.
explanation: 'In' shows the relationship between the action 'playing' and the noun 'garden,' indicating the location of the activity. This makes it a preposition. Prepositions are words that connect a noun or pronoun to other words in a sentence, typically indicating relationships of location, direction, time, or manner. They usually introduce a prepositional phrase.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: He is poor **but** he is very honest.
explanation:
'But' connects two contrasting clauses ('He is poor' and 'he is very honest'), indicating opposition or contrast. This function identifies it as a conjunction. Conjunctions are words used to connect words, phrases, clauses, or sentences, creating relationships between different parts of a sentence. They can be coordinating (like 'but', 'and', 'or') or subordinating.
Rule 3: The "Hardly / Scarcely" Rule
"Hardly" and "Scarcely" mean "almost not" and are strictly followed by when or before (never 'than'). Like "no sooner," they take an inverted verb structure.
* Exam Error: Hardly had he started speaking than the mic broke. (❌)
* Correction: Hardly had he started speaking when the mic broke. (✅)
Rule 4: The "Although / Though" Rule
These words show contrast. They are followed by yet or simply a comma (,). They are never followed by "but".
* Exam Error: Although he is rich, but he is unhappy. (❌)
* Correction: Although he is rich, yet he is unhappy. (✅) or Although he is rich**,** he is unhappy. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Alas!** The great leader is no more.
explanation:
'Alas' expresses sudden sorrow or grief, which is the primary function of an interjection. Interjections are words or short phrases that express strong emotion or sudden feeling, often standing alone or at the beginning of a sentence. They typically have no grammatical connection to the rest of the sentence and are followed by an exclamation mark.
Rule 1: Words of Sorrow ("Alas", "Oh")
Remove "Alas!" and change the reporting verb to "exclaimed with sorrow" or "exclaimed with grief".
Direct: The old man said, "Alas! I am ruined."
Indirect: The old man exclaimed with sorrow that he was ruined. (✅)
Rule 2: Words of Joy ("Hurrah", "Wow")
Remove "Hurrah!" and change the reporting verb to "exclaimed with joy" or "exclaimed joyfully".
Direct: The boys said, "Hurrah! We have won the cup."
Indirect: The boys exclaimed with joy that they had won the cup. (✅)
Rule 3: Words of Praise ("Bravo")
Remove "Bravo!" and change the reporting verb to "applauded", often followed by "saying that".
Direct: The captain said to the player, "Bravo! You played brilliantly."
Indirect: The captain applauded the player, saying that he had played brilliantly. (✅)
Rule 4: Words of Disgust or Contempt ("Ugh", "Pooh", "Fie")
Remove the interjection and change the reporting verb to "exclaimed with disgust" or "exclaimed with contempt".
Direct: She said, "Ugh! There is a fly in my soup."
Indirect: She exclaimed with disgust that there was a fly in her soup. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: I saw **an** elephant walking down the road.
explanation: 'An' is an indefinite article used before a word starting with a vowel sound (elephant). Articles are a special type of adjective that determine whether a noun is specific or general. 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles, referring to non-specific items, while 'the' is a definite article, referring to specific items. They are crucial for clarity in English.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **They** will arrive at the station tomorrow morning.
explanation:
'They' is a personal pronoun used in place of a plural noun (e.g., 'the students,' 'my friends') to act as the subject of the sentence. Pronouns are words that replace nouns in a sentence to avoid repetition. Personal pronouns refer to specific people or things and vary based on person (first, second, third), number (singular, plural), gender, and case (subject, object, possessive).
Rule 2: The "Let" and "Preposition" Rule
After the word Let, or any preposition (like between, except, but, for), you must always use the Objective Case of the pronoun (e.g., me, him, her, us, them), never the Subjective Case (I, he, she, we, they).
Exam Error: Let he and I solve this paper. (❌)
Correction: Let him and me solve this paper. (✅)
Exam Error: There is no secret between you and I. (❌)
Correction: There is no secret between you and me. (✅)

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: His immense **courage** inspired everyone in the army.
explanation: "Courage" is an abstract noun representing a human quality.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The **information** provided by the guide was very helpful.
explanation: "Information" is an uncountable abstract noun.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The swimmer took a deep **breath** before diving in.
explanation: "Breath" is a noun, whereas "breathe" is the verb form. Here it acts as the object.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The students are **playing** chess in the sports room.
explanation: "Playing" is the present participle form of the main verb in this continuous tense sentence.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: He is an **elderly** gentleman who loves gardening.
explanation: Despite ending in "-ly," "elderly" describes the noun "gentleman," making it an adjective.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: I will submit the required documents **tomorrow**.
explanation: "Tomorrow" is an adverb of time, telling us when the action will happen.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: We have been living in this neighborhood **since** 2010.
explanation: "Since" is used here as a preposition of time to show the starting point of an action.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: I stayed home from work **because** I was feeling unwell.
explanation: "Because" connects the dependent reason clause to the independent main clause.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Hurrah**! We won the championship trophy.
explanation: "Hurrah" is an interjection used to express intense joy or victory.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **The** Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.
explanation: "The" is a definite article used before the specific name of an ocean.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Which** of these two historical books is yours?
explanation: "Which" acts as an interrogative pronoun taking the place of the noun being asked about.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: We **should** always respect our elders and teachers.
explanation: "Should" is a modal auxiliary verb indicating duty or advice.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: She was **very** happy with her final exam results.
explanation: "Very" is an adverb of degree modifying the adjective "happy."

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The manager finally gave **him** the office keys.
explanation: "Him" is an objective personal pronoun receiving the action of the verb.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: I drank some fresh **water** from the thermos flask.
explanation: In this sentence, "water" is the object (a thing) being consumed, making it a noun.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: Make sure to complete the assigned work **before** Monday.
explanation: "Before" shows a time relationship between the action and the noun "Monday."

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Both** Ram and Shyam are excellent cricket players.
explanation: "Both" acts as a part of the correlative conjunction pair "Both...and" to link two subjects.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: Please **water** the indoor plants every morning.
explanation: "Water" is a verb here, meaning to supply with water.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: She baked the delicious chocolate cake all by **herself**.
explanation: "Herself" is a reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject "She."

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: There are **several** reasons for this unexpected delay.
explanation: "Several" is an adjective of number modifying the noun "reasons."

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: It started raining heavily, so they went **inside**.
explanation: Here, "inside" modifies the verb "went" indicating the place/direction of the action.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: The missing keys were found **under** the living room sofa.
explanation: "Under" shows the spatial relationship between the "keys" and the "sofa."

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: You can either study for the test **or** watch television.
explanation: "Or" is a coordinating conjunction offering an alternative between two actions.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: **Ouch**! I stepped on a sharp piece of glass.
explanation: "Ouch" expresses sudden pain, which is the role of an interjection.

content: Identify the part of speech of the highlighted word: It takes approximately **an** hour to reach the railway station.
explanation: "An" is an indefinite article used before "hour" because it starts with a vowel sound (silent 'h').

content: Identify the type of noun in the sentence: "Honesty is the best policy."
explanation: Honesty refers to a quality or state rather than a concrete object, making it an abstract noun.

content: Choose the synonym for 'Diligent'.
explanation: 'Diligent' means having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties, which is synonymous with 'industrious'.

content: Choose the antonym for 'Benevolent'.
explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly. Its opposite is 'malicious', meaning intending or intended to do harm.

content: Choose the antonym for 'Exacerbate'.
explanation: 'Exacerbate' means to make (a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling) worse. Its opposite is 'alleviate', meaning to make suffering, deficiency, or a problem less severe.

Rearrange the following sentences (A), (B), (C), and (D) to form a coherent paragraph:
(A) It is imperative for students to understand their own learning styles.
(B) Some students grasp concepts better through visual aids, while others prefer auditory explanations.
(C) This self-awareness can significantly enhance their academic performance.
(D) Still others learn best through hands-on practical experience.
explanation: A introduces the main idea: understanding learning styles. B provides the first example of a learning style. D provides another example, logically following B. C concludes by stating the benefit of this self-awareness. The correct order is ABDC.

content:
Rearrange the following sentences (A), (B), (C), and (D) to form a coherent paragraph:
(A) The internet has revolutionized the way we access information.
(B) However, it also presents challenges such as misinformation and privacy concerns.
(C) It provides a vast repository of knowledge at our fingertips.
(D) Therefore, critical thinking and digital literacy are essential skills today.
explanation: A introduces the topic: internet revolutionizing information access. C expands on A, explaining how it provides knowledge. B introduces a contrasting point: challenges. D offers a conclusion/solution based on the challenges. The correct order is ACBD.

content: Choose the correct plural form of 'sheep'.
explanation: The plural form of 'sheep' is 'sheep' itself, as it is an irregular noun.

content:
Rearrange the following sentences (A), (B), (C), and (D) to form a coherent paragraph:
(A) For instance, proper diet and regular exercise are fundamental.
(B) Maintaining a healthy lifestyle requires consistent effort and discipline.
(C) Additionally, adequate sleep and stress management play crucial roles.
(D) Neglecting any of these aspects can lead to various health problems.
explanation: B introduces the main idea: maintaining a healthy lifestyle requires effort. A provides the first examples: diet and exercise. C adds more examples: sleep and stress management. D concludes by stating the consequence of neglecting these aspects. The correct order is BADC.

content: Fill in the blank with the correct pronoun: "Neither Rohan nor his friends submitted ______ assignments on time."
explanation: When 'neither...nor' connects two subjects, and the second subject is plural ('his friends'), the pronoun should agree with the nearer subject, which is plural.

content: Choose the correct pronoun to complete the sentence: "The dog, ______ had a collar, barked loudly."
explanation: 'Which' is used as a relative pronoun for animals and inanimate objects. 'Who' and 'whom' are for people.

content: Change the voice of the following sentence from active to passive: "The students are playing cricket."
options: Cricket is played by the students.
Cricket is being played by the students.
Cricket was played by the students.
Cricket has been played by the students.
explanation: The sentence is in the present continuous tense (are playing). In passive voice, it becomes 'is/are being + past participle'.

content: Change the voice of the following sentence from passive to active: "A letter was written by her."
explanation: The sentence is in the simple past passive voice (was written). The active voice counterpart is the simple past tense (subject + V2 + object).

content: Choose the one word that best describes: "A person who hates women."
explanation: A misogynist is a person who dislikes, despises, or is strongly prejudiced against women.

content: Choose the one word that best describes: "A place where birds are kept."
explanation: An aviary is a large enclosure for confining birds. An aquarium is for aquatic animals, an apiary for bees.

content: Choose the synonym for 'Candid'.
explanation: 'Candid' means truthful and straightforward, which is synonymous with 'frank'.

content: भारतीय राज्यघटनेच्या निर्मितीसाठी संविधान सभेची स्थापना कोणत्या योजनेअंतर्गत करण्यात आली?
explanation: भारतीय राज्यघटनेच्या निर्मितीसाठी जुलै १९४६ मध्ये 'कॅबिनेट मिशन योजना' (Cabinet Mission Plan) नुसार संविधान सभेची स्थापना करण्यात आली. या योजनेने भारतासाठी एक संघराज्य संरचना सुचवली आणि संविधान सभेची रचना निश्चित केली. संविधान सभेची पहिली बैठक ९ डिसेंबर १९४६ रोजी झाली.

content: राज्यपालांच्या नियुक्तीसाठी किमान वय किती असणे आवश्यक आहे?
explanation: राज्यपालांच्या नियुक्तीसाठी भारतीय संविधानाने विहित केलेली किमान वयोमर्यादा ३५ वर्षे आहे. राज्यपाल हे राज्याचे कार्यकारी प्रमुख असतात आणि त्यांची नियुक्ती राष्ट्रपतींकडून केली जाते. त्यांना राज्याचा मुख्यमंत्री आणि इतर मंत्र्यांना शपथ देण्याचा अधिकार असतो.

content: भारतीय संविधानाची 'उद्देशिका' (Preamble) कोणत्या देशाच्या संविधानावरून प्रेरित आहे?
explanation: भारतीय संविधानाची उद्देशिका अमेरिकेच्या संविधानाच्या उद्देशिकेतून प्रेरित आहे. 'आम्ही भारताचे लोक' (We, the People of India) ही संकल्पना अमेरिकन संविधानातून घेतली आहे. उद्देशिका हे भारतीय संविधानाचे सार आणि आत्मा मानले जाते, जे संविधानाची मूलभूत मूल्ये आणि उद्दिष्ट्ये दर्शवते.

content: राज्यघटनेच्या कोणत्या कलमांतर्गत 'राष्ट्रपती राजवट' (President's Rule) लागू केली जाते?
explanation: भारतीय राज्यघटनेच्या कलम ३५६ नुसार, एखाद्या राज्यातील संवैधानिक यंत्रणा कोलमडली असल्यास, राष्ट्रपती त्या राज्यात 'राष्ट्रपती राजवट' लागू करू शकतात. यालाच 'राज्य आणीबाणी' असेही म्हटले जाते. कलम ३५२ राष्ट्रीय आणीबाणी तर कलम ३६० आर्थिक आणीबाणीशी संबंधित आहे.

content: संसद सदस्य नसतानाही खालीलपैकी कोण संसदेच्या दोन्ही सभागृहात उपस्थित राहून बोलू शकतो?
explanation: भारताचा महान्यायवादी (Attorney General of India) हे संसद सदस्य नसतानाही संसदेच्या दोन्ही सभागृहात उपस्थित राहू शकतात आणि बोलू शकतात, परंतु त्यांना मतदानाचा अधिकार नसतो. ते केंद्र सरकारचे मुख्य कायदेशीर सल्लागार असतात आणि त्यांची नियुक्ती राष्ट्रपती करतात. हे कलम ७६ मध्ये नमूद केले आहे.

content: भारतीय संविधानाच्या कोणत्या परिशिष्टात (Schedule) केंद्र आणि राज्यांमध्ये कायदेशीर शक्तींच्या वितरणाशी संबंधित तरतुदी आहेत?
explanation: भारतीय संविधानाच्या सातव्या परिशिष्टात (Seventh Schedule) केंद्र सरकार आणि राज्य सरकार यांच्यातील कायदेशीर शक्तींच्या वितरणाशी संबंधित तरतुदी आहेत. यामध्ये तीन सूचींचा समावेश आहे: संघ सूची (Union List), राज्य सूची (State List) आणि समवर्ती सूची (Concurrent List).

content: कोणत्या घटनादुरुस्तीद्वारे मतदानाचे वय २१ वर्षांवरून १८ वर्षांपर्यंत कमी करण्यात आले?
explanation: ६१व्या घटनादुरुस्ती कायदा, १९८९ द्वारे लोकसभेच्या आणि राज्य विधानसभांच्या निवडणुकांसाठी मतदानाचे वय २१ वर्षांवरून १८ वर्षांपर्यंत कमी करण्यात आले. या दुरुस्तीमुळे भारतीय लोकशाहीमध्ये अधिक युवा मतदारांचा सहभाग सुनिश्चित झाला.

content: भारतीय संविधानातील 'न्यायिक पुनर्विलोकन' (Judicial Review) ही संकल्पना कोणत्या देशाकडून स्वीकारली आहे?
explanation: भारतीय संविधानातील 'न्यायिक पुनर्विलोकन' (Judicial Review) ही संकल्पना अमेरिकेच्या संविधानातून स्वीकारली आहे. या संकल्पनेनुसार, न्यायपालिका संसद किंवा विधिमंडळाने बनवलेले कायदे संविधानाला अनुसरून आहेत की नाही, हे तपासू शकते आणि ते संविधानाच्या विरुद्ध असल्यास रद्द करू शकते.

content: खालीलपैकी कोणते मूलभूत हक्क परदेशी नागरिकांना उपलब्ध नाहीत?
explanation: कलम १५ (धर्म, वंश, जात, लिंग किंवा जन्मस्थान यांवर आधारित भेदभावाला प्रतिबंध), कलम १६ (सार्वजनिक रोजगाराच्या बाबतीत समान संधी), कलम १९ (अभिव्यक्ती स्वातंत्र्याचा हक्क) आणि कलम २९ (अल्पसंख्याकांचे सांस्कृतिक व शैक्षणिक हक्क) हे मूलभूत हक्क केवळ भारतीय नागरिकांनाच उपलब्ध आहेत. परदेशी नागरिकांना 'जीवनाचा आणि वैयक्तिक स्वातंत्र्याचा हक्क' (कलम २१) यासारखे काही हक्क उपलब्ध आहेत.

content: भारतीय संविधानाच्या कोणत्या कलमांतर्गत राज्यघटनेत दुरुस्ती (Amendment) केली जाते?
explanation: भारतीय संविधानाच्या भाग २० मधील कलम ३६८ नुसार, संसदेला संविधानात दुरुस्ती करण्याचा अधिकार आहे. ही दुरुस्ती दोन प्रकारांनी करता येते: संसदेतील विशेष बहुमताने किंवा संसदेतील विशेष बहुमताने आणि राज्यांच्या निम्म्या विधानमंडळांच्या सहमतीने.

content: राष्ट्रीय आणीबाणी (National Emergency) घोषित करण्यासाठी खालीलपैकी कोणते कारण असू शकत नाही?
explanation: भारतीय राज्यघटनेच्या कलम ३५२ नुसार, 'युद्ध', 'बाह्य आक्रमण' किंवा 'सशस्त्र बंड' (Armed Rebellion) या कारणांवरून राष्ट्रपती राष्ट्रीय आणीबाणी घोषित करू शकतात. मूळतः 'अंतर्गत अशांतता' (Internal Disturbance) हे कारण होते, परंतु ४४व्या घटनादुरुस्तीने ते बदलून 'सशस्त्र बंड' असे करण्यात आले. 'आर्थिक अस्थिरता' हे कारण राष्ट्रीय आणीबाणीसाठी नाही, तर ते 'आर्थिक आणीबाणी' (कलम ३६०) साठीचे कारण असू शकते.

content: भारतीय राज्यघटनेतील 'धर्मनिरपेक्ष' (Secular) हा शब्द कोणत्या घटनादुरुस्तीद्वारे समाविष्ट करण्यात आला?
explanation: भारतीय राज्यघटनेच्या उद्देशिकेत 'धर्मनिरपेक्ष' (Secular) हा शब्द ४२व्या घटनादुरुस्ती, १९७६ द्वारे समाविष्ट करण्यात आला. या दुरुस्तीद्वारे 'समाजवादी' (Socialist) आणि 'अखंडता' (Integrity) हे शब्दही उद्देशिकेत समाविष्ट करण्यात आले, ज्यामुळे भारतीय लोकशाहीचे समाजवादी आणि धर्मनिरपेक्ष स्वरूप अधिक स्पष्ट झाले.

content: भारतीय संविधानातील 'मूलभूत संरचनेचा सिद्धांत' (Basic Structure Doctrine) कोणत्या खटल्यातून उदयास आला?
options: केशवानंद भारती विरुद्ध केरळ राज्य खटला
मिनर्वा मिल्स विरुद्ध भारत सरकार खटला
इंदिरा साहनी विरुद्ध भारत सरकार खटला
explanation: केशवानंद भारती खटला, १९७३ मध्ये सर्वोच्च न्यायालयाने 'मूलभूत संरचनेचा सिद्धांत' मांडला. या सिद्धांतानुसार, संसद संविधानाच्या कोणत्याही भागात दुरुस्ती करू शकते, परंतु संविधानाच्या मूलभूत संरचनेत बदल करू शकत नाही. या खटल्यामुळे संसदेच्या घटनादुरुस्तीच्या अधिकारावर मर्यादा आल्या.

content: पंचायतराज संस्थांना संवैधानिक दर्जा कोणत्या घटनादुरुस्तीद्वारे मिळाला?
explanation: ७३व्या घटनादुरुस्ती कायदा, १९९२ द्वारे पंचायतराज संस्थांना संवैधानिक दर्जा प्राप्त झाला. या दुरुस्तीने संविधानात भाग IX आणि ११वे परिशिष्ट समाविष्ट केले, ज्यामुळे ग्रामीण स्थानिक स्वराज्य संस्थांना बळकटी मिळाली. या दुरुस्तीने पंचायतराज संस्थांना नियमित निवडणुका, आर्थिक स्वायत्तता आणि विकासाची जबाबदारी दिली.

content: भारतीय नियंत्रक आणि महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG) यांचा मुख्य कार्यकाळ किती असतो?
explanation: भारतीय नियंत्रक आणि महालेखा परीक्षक (CAG) यांचा मुख्य कार्यकाळ ६ वर्षे किंवा ६५ वर्षांचे वय पूर्ण होईपर्यंत असतो, यापैकी जे आधी येईल ते लागू होते. ते सार्वजनिक निधीचे प्रमुख संरक्षक असतात आणि केंद्र व राज्य सरकारांच्या खर्चाचे लेखापरीक्षण करतात. त्यांची नियुक्ती राष्ट्रपती करतात.

content: 'शिक्षणाचा अधिकार' (Right to Education) हे मूलभूत हक्क म्हणून कोणत्या घटनादुरुस्तीद्वारे समाविष्ट करण्यात आले?
explanation: ८६व्या घटनादुरुस्ती कायदा, २००२ द्वारे 'शिक्षणाचा अधिकार' (Right to Education) भारतीय संविधानात मूलभूत हक्क म्हणून समाविष्ट करण्यात आला. या दुरुस्तीने कलम २१-A समाविष्ट केले, ज्यानुसार राज्य ६ ते १४ वयोगटातील सर्व मुलांना मोफत आणि सक्तीचे शिक्षण देईल. तसेच, कलम ५१-A मध्ये नवीन ११वे मूलभूत कर्तव्य जोडले.

content: राष्ट्रपती लोकसभेत अँग्लो-इंडियन समुदायाचे किती सदस्य नामनिर्देशित करू शकत होते (सध्या रद्द)?
explanation: मूळतः, राष्ट्रपती लोकसभेत अँग्लो-इंडियन समुदायाचे २ सदस्य नामनिर्देशित करू शकत होते, जर त्यांना सभागृहात पुरेसे प्रतिनिधित्व मिळाले नसेल तर. मात्र, १०४व्या घटनादुरुस्ती कायदा, २०१९ द्वारे हे प्रावधान रद्द करण्यात आले आहे. त्यामुळे आता अँग्लो-इंडियन सदस्यांच्या नामनिर्देशनाची तरतूद नाही.

content: भारतीय संविधानाच्या कोणत्या परिशिष्टात पक्षांतरबंदी कायद्याची (Anti-Defection Law) तरतूद आहे?
explanation: भारतीय संविधानाच्या १०व्या परिशिष्टात (Tenth Schedule) पक्षांतरबंदी कायद्याची (Anti-Defection Law) तरतूद आहे. हे परिशिष्ट ५२व्या घटनादुरुस्ती, १९८५ द्वारे संविधानात समाविष्ट करण्यात आले. आमदार आणि खासदारांना एका पक्षातून दुसऱ्या पक्षात जाण्यापासून रोखणे हा या कायद्याचा मुख्य उद्देश आहे, जेणेकरून राजकीय अस्थिरता टाळता येईल.

content: भारतीय संविधानाचा कोणता भाग मूलभूत हक्कांशी (Fundamental Rights) संबंधित आहे?
explanation: भारतीय संविधानाच्या तिसऱ्या भागात (Part III) नागरिकांचे मूलभूत हक्क नमूद केलेले आहेत. हे हक्क नागरिकांच्या सर्वांगीण विकासासाठी आवश्यक मानले जातात आणि ते न्यायप्रविष्ट (Justiciable) आहेत, म्हणजे त्यांच्या उल्लंघनाच्या बाबतीत नागरिक न्यायालयात दाद मागू शकतात.

content: खालीलपैकी कोणते मार्गदर्शक तत्त्व (Directive Principle) ४२व्या घटनादुरुस्तीने समाविष्ट करण्यात आले नाही?
options: समान न्याय आणि मोफत कायदेशीर सहाय्य
explanation: ४२व्या घटनादुरुस्ती, १९७६ ने 'उद्योगधंद्यांच्या व्यवस्थापनात कामगारांचा सहभाग' (कलम 43A), 'बालकांच्या निरोगी विकासासाठी संधी' (कलम 39(f)), आणि 'पर्यावरणाचे संरक्षण व सुधारणा' (कलम 48A) ही मार्गदर्शक तत्त्वे समाविष्ट केली. 'समान न्याय आणि मोफत कायदेशीर सहाय्य' (कलम 39A) हे देखील ४२व्या दुरुस्तीनेच समाविष्ट केले. तर 'ग्रामपंचायतींचे संघटन' (कलम ४०) हे मूळ राज्यघटनेतच समाविष्ट होते.

content: भारतीय नागरिकांसाठी एकूण किती मूलभूत कर्तव्ये (Fundamental Duties) संविधानात नमूद केलेली आहेत?
explanation: भारतीय संविधानाच्या भाग IV-A मध्ये, कलम ५१-A अंतर्गत नागरिकांची एकूण ११ मूलभूत कर्तव्ये नमूद केलेली आहेत. मूळतः, १९७६ मध्ये ४२व्या घटनादुरुस्तीद्वारे १० कर्तव्ये समाविष्ट करण्यात आली होती. त्यानंतर, २००२ मध्ये ८६व्या घटनादुरुस्तीद्वारे 'सहा ते चौदा वयोगटातील मुलांना शिक्षणाची संधी उपलब्ध करून देणे' हे ११वे कर्तव्य समाविष्ट करण्यात आले.

content: भारतीय राष्ट्रपतींचा निवडणूक गण (Electoral College) खालीलपैकी कोणाचा समावेश असतो?
options: केवळ लोकसभेचे आणि राज्यसभेचे निवडून आलेले सदस्य
संसद आणि राज्य विधानसभेचे निवडून आलेले सदस्य
explanation: भारतीय राष्ट्रपतींच्या निवडणुकीत संसद आणि राज्य विधानसभांमधील निवडून आलेले सदस्य भाग घेतात. यामध्ये लोकसभेचे निवडून आलेले सदस्य, राज्यसभेचे निवडून आलेले सदस्य आणि राज्यांच्या विधानसभांमधील निवडून आलेले सदस्य यांचा समावेश असतो. विधान परिषदेचे सदस्य आणि नामनिर्देशित सदस्य मतदानात भाग घेत नाहीत.

content: राज्यसभेचा पदसिद्ध अध्यक्ष (Ex-officio Chairman) कोण असतो?
explanation: भारताचे उपराष्ट्रपती हे राज्यसभेचे पदसिद्ध अध्यक्ष असतात. ते राज्यसभेच्या कामकाजाचे अध्यक्षपद भूषवतात आणि सभागृहात शिस्त व सुव्यवस्था राखतात. मात्र, उपराष्ट्रपती हे राज्यसभेचे सदस्य नसतात.

content: भारतात संसदेचे संयुक्त अधिवेशन (Joint Sitting) कोण बोलावू शकते?
explanation: भारतीय राज्यघटनेच्या कलम १०८ नुसार, दोन्ही सभागृहांमध्ये (लोकसभा आणि राज्यसभा) एखाद्या सामान्य विधेयकावर मतभेद निर्माण झाल्यास, राष्ट्रपती संसदेचे संयुक्त अधिवेशन बोलावू शकतात. या अधिवेशनाची अध्यक्षता लोकसभेचे अध्यक्ष करतात.

content: भारतीय संविधानाच्या कोणत्या कलमामध्ये 'घटनात्मक उपायांचा हक्क' (Right to Constitutional Remedies) समाविष्ट आहे?
explanation: कलम ३२ हे 'घटनात्मक उपायांच्या हक्काशी' संबंधित आहे, ज्याला डॉ. बाबासाहेब आंबेडकरांनी भारतीय संविधानाचा 'आत्मा आणि हृदय' म्हटले आहे. हे कलम नागरिकांना त्यांच्या मूलभूत हक्कांच्या संरक्षणासाठी थेट सर्वोच्च न्यायालयात जाण्याचा अधिकार देते आणि न्यायालयास विविध रिट (writ) जारी करण्याचा अधिकार देते.

content: महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात लांब नदी कोणती?
explanation: गोदावरी ही महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात लांब नदी असून, ती नाशिक जिल्ह्यातील त्र्यंबकेश्वर येथे उगम पावते. महाराष्ट्रात तिचा प्रवाह सुमारे ६६८ किमी आहे, ज्यामुळे ती राज्याच्या अनेक भागांना जलपुरवठा करते.

content: कोयना, वारणा आणि वेण्णा या कोणत्या नदीच्या प्रमुख उपनद्या आहेत?
explanation: कोयना, वारणा आणि वेण्णा या कृष्णा नदीच्या महत्त्वाच्या उपनद्या आहेत. कोयना नदीवर कोयना धरण असून ते महाराष्ट्रासाठी महत्त्वाचे आहे.

content: तोतलाडोह धरण कोणत्या नदीवर आणि कोणत्या जिल्ह्यात आहे?
explanation: तोतलाडोह धरण हे वर्धा नदीवर नागपूर जिल्ह्यात आहे. या धरणाला 'मेघदूत जलाशय' असेही म्हणतात आणि ते महाराष्ट्राच्या विदर्भ भागासाठी महत्त्वपूर्ण आहे.

content: खालीलपैकी कोणती नदी अरबी समुद्राला मिळते?
explanation: तापी नदी पूर्वेकडून पश्चिमेकडे वाहत जाऊन थेट अरबी समुद्राला मिळते. गोदावरी, कृष्णा आणि भीमा या नद्या बंगालच्या उपसागराला मिळतात.

content: भीमा नदीचा उगम कोणत्या पर्वतरांगांमध्ये होतो?
explanation: भीमा नदीचा उगम पुणे जिल्ह्यातील भीमाशंकर येथे सह्याद्री पर्वतरांगांमध्ये होतो. भीमाशंकर हे एक ज्योतिर्लिंग ठिकाण आहे.

content: महाराष्ट्रातील 'नाथसागर' या नावाने कोणत्या धरणाच्या जलाशयास ओळखले जाते?
explanation: औरंगाबाद जिल्ह्यातील गोदावरी नदीवरील जायकवाडी धरणाच्या जलाशयाला 'नाथसागर' असे ओळखले जाते. हे धरण मराठवाड्यासाठी महत्त्वाचे आहे.

content: नाशिक शहर कोणत्या नदीच्या काठी वसलेले आहे?
explanation: नाशिक शहर गोदावरी नदीच्या काठी वसलेले आहे. गोदावरी नदीचा उगम नाशिक जिल्ह्यातील त्र्यंबकेश्वर येथे होतो आणि कुंभमेळ्यासाठी हे शहर प्रसिद्ध आहे.

content: पैनगंगा, वर्धा आणि वैनगंगा या नद्या कोणत्या दिशेने वाहतात आणि कोणत्या नदीला मिळतात?
explanation: पैनगंगा, वर्धा आणि वैनगंगा या गोदावरीच्या प्रमुख उपनद्या असून त्या पूर्वेकडे वाहत जाऊन गोदावरी नदीला मिळतात. वर्धा आणि वैनगंगा एकत्र येऊन प्राणहिता नदी बनवतात, जी नंतर गोदावरीला मिळते.

content: उजनी धरण कोणत्या नदीवर बांधले आहे आणि ते प्रामुख्याने कोणत्या कामासाठी वापरले जाते?
explanation: उजनी धरण भीमा नदीवर सोलापूर जिल्ह्यात बांधले आहे. याचा उपयोग प्रामुख्याने सिंचनासाठी आणि सोलापूर जिल्ह्याला पिण्याच्या पाण्याचा पुरवठा करण्यासाठी होतो.

content: महाराष्ट्रामधील दुसऱ्या क्रमांकाचे सर्वात मोठे नदी खोरे कोणत्या नदीचे आहे?
explanation: गोदावरी नदीच्या खोऱ्यानंतर कृष्णा नदीचे खोरे महाराष्ट्रातील दुसऱ्या क्रमांकाचे सर्वात मोठे खोरे आहे. कृष्णा खोरे हे पश्चिम महाराष्ट्राच्या मोठ्या भागाला व्यापते.

content: अमरावती जिल्ह्यातून वाहणाऱ्या आणि तापी नदीला मिळणाऱ्या प्रमुख उपनदीचे नाव काय?
explanation: पूर्णा नदी ही तापी नदीची एक महत्त्वाची उपनदी आहे जी अमरावती जिल्ह्यातून वाहते. ती तापी खोऱ्याचा एक महत्त्वाचा भाग आहे.

content: कृष्णा नदीचा उगम महाराष्ट्रातील कोणत्या जिल्ह्यात होतो?
explanation: कृष्णा नदीचा उगम सातारा जिल्ह्यातील महाबळेश्वर येथे होतो. महाबळेश्वर हे थंड हवेचे ठिकाण असून तेथून अनेक नद्या उगम पावतात, त्यापैकी कृष्णा ही एक प्रमुख नदी आहे.

content: सह्याद्री पर्वतरांग ही महाराष्ट्रातील नद्यांसाठी कशाचे कार्य करते?
explanation: सह्याद्री पर्वतरांग ही महाराष्ट्रातील अनेक नद्यांचे उगमस्थान असून, ती अरबी समुद्राला मिळणाऱ्या नद्या आणि बंगालच्या उपसागराला मिळणाऱ्या नद्या यांना विभाजित करते, त्यामुळे तिला 'जलविभाजक' असे म्हणतात.

content: गोदावरी नदीची महाराष्ट्रातील एकूण लांबी अंदाजे किती किलोमीटर आहे?
explanation: गोदावरी नदीची महाराष्ट्रातील एकूण लांबी अंदाजे ६६८ किलोमीटर आहे. त्यानंतर ती तेलंगणा आणि आंध्र प्रदेशातून प्रवास करून बंगालच्या उपसागराला मिळते.

content: प्रवरा, मुळा, दारणा आणि कादवा या कोणत्या नदीच्या प्रमुख उपनद्या आहेत?
explanation: प्रवरा, मुळा, दारणा आणि कादवा या गोदावरी नदीच्या प्रमुख उपनद्या आहेत. या नद्या गोदावरीच्या खोऱ्यात मोठा जलभाग आणतात.

content: पुणे शहर कोणत्या दोन नद्यांच्या संगमावर वसलेले आहे?
explanation: पुणे शहर मुळा आणि मुठा या दोन नद्यांच्या संगमावर वसलेले आहे. या नद्या पुढे भीमा नदीला मिळतात.

content: अप्पर वर्धा प्रकल्प कोणत्या जिल्ह्यात स्थित आहे?
explanation: अप्पर वर्धा प्रकल्प अमरावती जिल्ह्यात मोर्शी तालुक्यात वर्धा नदीवर बांधला आहे. हा प्रकल्प अमरावती आणि वर्धा जिल्ह्यांना सिंचनासाठी आणि पिण्याच्या पाण्याचा पुरवठा करतो.

content: विदर्भात प्रामुख्याने कोणत्या नदी प्रणालीचे वर्चस्व आहे?
explanation: विदर्भामध्ये गोदावरी नदी प्रणालीचे मोठे वर्चस्व आहे, विशेषतः तिच्या वैनगंगा आणि वर्धा या प्रमुख उपनद्यांच्या प्रणालीमुळे. या नद्या विदर्भाच्या मोठ्या भागातून वाहतात.

content: गिरणा नदी कोणत्या प्रमुख नदीची उपनदी आहे?
explanation: गिरणा नदी ही तापी नदीची एक महत्त्वाची उपनदी आहे. ती नाशिक जिल्ह्यातून उगम पावते आणि जळगाव जिल्ह्यात तापी नदीला मिळते, ज्यामुळे उत्तर महाराष्ट्राला जलपुरवठा होतो.

content: खालीलपैकी कोणती नदी पूर्वेकडे वाहत नाही?
explanation: तापी नदी पूर्वेकडून पश्चिमेकडे वाहत जाऊन अरबी समुद्राला मिळते. याउलट, गोदावरी, भीमा आणि कृष्णा या प्रमुख नद्या पूर्वेकडे वाहत जाऊन बंगालच्या उपसागराला मिळतात.

content: पूर्णा नदी ही कोणत्या प्रमुख नदीची उपनदी आहे?
explanation: पूर्णा नदी ही तापी नदीची एक महत्त्वाची उपनदी आहे. ती मध्य प्रदेशातून उगम पावून महाराष्ट्रातून वाहत तापी नदीला मिळते, ज्यामुळे तापी खोऱ्याचा विस्तार होतो.

content: जायकवाडी धरण कोणत्या नदीवर बांधले आहे?
explanation: जायकवाडी धरण हे गोदावरी नदीवर औरंगाबाद जिल्ह्यात पैठणजवळ बांधले आहे. या धरणाच्या जलाशयाला 'नाथसागर' असेही म्हणतात आणि ते मराठवाड्यासाठी महत्त्वाचे जलसाधन आहे.

content: पंढरपूर हे तीर्थक्षेत्र कोणत्या नदीच्या काठी वसलेले आहे?
explanation: पंढरपूर हे महाराष्ट्रातील एक महत्त्वाचे तीर्थक्षेत्र असून ते भीमा नदीच्या काठी वसलेले आहे. भीमा नदीला येथे 'चंद्रभागा' या नावानेही ओळखले जाते कारण ती अर्धचंद्राकृती वळण घेते.

content: भीमा नदीच्या प्रमुख उपनद्यांपैकी एक नसलेली नदी कोणती?
explanation: वर्धा नदी ही भीमा नदीची उपनदी नाही, तर ती गोदावरी नदीच्या प्रमुख उपनद्यांपैकी एक आहे. नीरा, मुळा आणि पवना या भीमा नदीच्या महत्त्वाच्या उपनद्या आहेत.

content: गोदावरी नदीचा उगम कोठे होतो?
explanation: गोदावरी नदीचा उगम नाशिक जिल्ह्यातील त्र्यंबकेश्वर येथे ब्रह्मगिरी पर्वतावर होतो. हे ठिकाण बारा ज्योतिर्लिंगांपैकी एक म्हणूनही प्रसिद्ध आहे.

content: महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात मोठे नदी खोरे कोणत्या नदीचे आहे?
explanation: गोदावरी नदीचे खोरे महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात मोठे नदी खोरे आहे, जे राज्याच्या सुमारे ४९% क्षेत्र व्यापते. यामुळे मराठवाडा आणि विदर्भाच्या काही भागांना लाभ होतो.

content:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error:

Having failed to receive (A) adequate support (B) from the students, (C) the principal decided to close the project. (D) No error (E)
options: the principal decided to close the project.
explanation: The error is in part (A). 'Having failed' is grammatically correct as a perfect participle indicating an action completed before the main action. However, the phrasing 'failed to receive' is correct. The sentence is grammatically sound. So, the answer should be (E) No error. Let's re-evaluate. The construction 'Having failed to receive' is a perfect participial phrase which correctly modifies 'the principal'. There is no grammatical or contextual error. content:

explanation: The phrase 'be used to' is followed by a V-ing (gerund) to express habitual action or familiarity. So, 'is used to getting up' is the correct form. 'Used to' followed by base verb (get up) refers to a past habit that no longer occurs.

content:
Change the voice of the following sentence:

Who broke the window?
options: The window was broken by whom?

content:
Change the narration of the following sentence:

The teacher said to the students, "Do your homework."
options: The teacher asked the students if they did their homework.
The teacher ordered the students to do their homework.
The teacher told the students that they should do their homework.
The teacher requested the students to do their homework.
explanation: This is an imperative sentence. When changing an imperative sentence in direct speech to indirect speech, the reporting verb changes to 'ordered', 'advised', 'requested', 'told', etc., and the imperative mood is replaced by 'to' + infinitive. Since it's a command/instruction, 'ordered' or 'told' is appropriate. So, 'The teacher ordered the students to do their homework.'

content:

She is writing a letter.
options: A letter was written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
A letter has been written by her.
A letter is written by her.

content:
Change the narration of the following sentence:

options: He said that he was going to Mumbai the next day.

The pronoun 'I' changes to 'he' (referring to the speaker). The Present Continuous 'am going' changes to Past Continuous 'was going'. 'Tomorrow' changes to 'the next day' or 'the following day'. Therefore, 'He said that he was going to Mumbai the next day.'

content:
The following sentence has an error in its tense. Identify the error and select the correct sentence from the options.
Sentence: If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allow you to go.
options: If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would allow you to go.
If you can apprise me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
explanation: This is a Type 3 conditional sentence (past unreal conditional), which describes a hypothetical situation in the past and its hypothetical past consequence. The correct structure for such sentences is: 'If + Subject + had + past participle (V3), Subject + would have + past participle (V3)'. In the given sentence, the first clause 'If you had apprised me about your problem earlier' correctly uses the past perfect tense. However, the second clause 'I would have allow you to go' incorrectly uses the base form of the verb 'allow'. It should be the past participle 'allowed'. Therefore, the correct sentence is 'If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.'
